conviction_note: Q3 is likely to land inside the guide ($215-230m, adj EBITDA $26-31m), since Ribbon hit its Q1 and Q2 revenue guides. The reaction turns on Q4 and the FY outlook ($810-840m implies Q4 of about $240-255m). Rosenblatt's 14 Sep downgrade on a further Verizon voice-modernization delay makes a FY cut more likely than not, but the stock is down 24% over 20 days and sits 3% above its 52-week low, so much of that is in the price. The lean is mildly negative (p_up 42) on a large absolute move (15%, the name's median reaction being 13.75% with 5 of 7 down). The findings' sum (-1.7) and the scaled number (-2.4) agree in sign.

findings.finding: Rosenblatt (analyst Mike Genovese) cut RBBN from Buy to Neutral on 2026-09-14, PT $3.50 to $2.20, because Verizon's voice-modernization project, the expected near-term catalyst, is delayed again and other Tier 1 carriers are not launching their own programs. The FY2026 guide of $810-840m already assumed a 'more moderated view' of US Tier 1 voice modernization, but it still needs an implied Q4 of about $240-255m against Q2's $192m, so a further Verizon delay points at a cut to the FY/Q4 outlook in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cuts and misses have been sold hard: -27.94% on 2026-02-05 (initial FY26 guide below expectations), -8.46% on 2026-04-28, -13.75% on 2025-10-22. On 2026-07-28 the FY guide was cut to $810-840m and the stock still rose 6.83%, because Q3 was guided up sequentially and IP Optical bookings hit a record.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell from about $2 to $1.37 after the downgrade, roughly a 30% drawdown. What is not visible is the size of any FY cut. If a cut to about $780-800m were fully priced, sell-side estimates would have been reset (consensus Q3 revenue still sits at the guide midpoint, $222-225m) and the stock would not still carry a guide-implied EV/EBITDA of about 6.5x.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K's own 'more moderated view' of US Tier 1 voice modernization, plus third-party call summaries saying Cloud & Edge fell 19% y/y on lower Verizon sales (https://www.panabee.com/news/ribbon-communications-earnings-q2-2026-report). The headline is confirmed separately by MarketScreener/MT Newswires on 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/ribbon-communications-shares-fall-after-rosenblatt-securities-downgrade-ce785bddd189f02c).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first covenant test after a waiver. On 2026-05-05 the First Amendment and Limited Waiver (HPS as agent) waived the Q2 net leverage test, set the Q3 maximum at 4.50x and 4.00x after that, and raised the margin to 7.00% in any quarter above 3.75x. Ribbon reported 4.0x net leverage at Q2, $338m term debt at 9.9%, cash of $43.5m (from $96.4m at year end), H1 operating cash flow of -$33.5m and $71m of receivables factored in H1. The money funds no ramp; it is covenant pressure. A Q3 EBITDA shortfall of about $10m would put leverage near 4.4-4.5x, and the Q4 step-down to 4.00x needs the FY EBITDA guide to hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The Q1 print (2026-04-28, -8.46%) came a week before the waiver was signed.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: market cap is about $245m against about $295m of net debt, and the equity trades like a stressed name. What is not priced is whether Q3 brings a second amendment, an equity raise or a liquidity update with the print. If it were fully priced, the stock would have held up after the October lows rather than making new ones near $1.32.
findings.independence: The amendment terms are in the Q1 10-Q and are summarised separately at https://www.panabee.com/news/ribbon-communications-earnings-q2-2026-report. Same company documents, so this counts as one source. The leverage arithmetic is inference, sized small.

findings.finding: In the Q2 release (2026-07-28), IP Optical bookings hit an all-time high led by North America. Call summaries put the book-to-bill at 1.6x and IP Optical revenue at $82m, up 30% sequentially, with defense-related revenue up about 60% sequentially. That supports the sequential ramp to the $215-230m Q3 guide coming from the segment (about 40% of revenue) that is not exposed to Verizon voice.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The record bookings were part of why the 2026-07-28 print rose 6.83% despite the FY cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has fallen 30% since that release on the Verizon story alone. The price weights the Cloud & Edge/Verizon miss and gives no visible credit for IP Optical backlog converting. If it did, the stock would not sit at its 52-week low into a quarter guided up 12-20% sequentially. Net of the rest of the company: Cloud & Edge (about 60%) has to hold roughly flat for this to show in total revenue.
findings.independence: Nokia's Q3 (2026-10-22) shows the same industry direction (separate finding below). Summary of the 1.6x figure: https://quartr.com/events/ribbon-communications-inc-rbbn-q2-2026_3YgjkVwv

findings.finding: Nokia's Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-22, after Ribbon last spoke) showed IP Networks sales up 43% at constant currency and Optical up 18%, with Network Infrastructure up 15% and a 2027 guide of +25-30% for combined Optical and IP. IP routing and optical demand was strong through the quarter Ribbon is reporting.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of RBBN reacting to peer prints.
findings.why_not_priced: RBBN fell further after Nokia's print, so the market is not reading it across. That is partly right: Nokia's growth is driven by AI and hyperscaler customers, while Ribbon sells to telcos, federal agencies and India.
findings.independence: Proxy. It shares its direction with Ribbon's own record IP Optical bookings, but it is a different company. https://convergedigest.com/nokia-reports-9-q3-net-sales-growth-driven-by-optical-and-cloud-segments/

findings.finding: Ribbon has delivered on its current-quarter guides this year: Q1 revenue $162.6m against a $160-170m guide, Q2 revenue $192.3m against $185-195m and Q2 adj EBITDA $12m against $9-14m. A Q3 inside $215-230m is the base case. The reported quarter is therefore unlikely to be the surprise; the forward guide is.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In-guide quarters drew -8.46% (Q1, on margins and the FY) and +6.83% (Q2, on bookings and the Q3 guide). The quarter itself has not decided the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced as a base case. It lands inside what the company guided, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001708055/000110465926087534/tm2621444d1_ex99-1.htm) is the other document. Both are company releases.

findings.finding: Verizon's Q3 2026 8-K shows $11.9bn of capex for the first nine months against its reaffirmed FY range of $16.0-16.5bn (from Q2), implying about $4.1-4.6bn in Q4. There is no sign of a capex cut at Ribbon's largest Cloud & Edge customer, but the program-specific voice-modernization timing is not visible in aggregate capex.
findings.why_not_priced: Neutral. Aggregate carrier capex does not resolve the Ribbon-specific project timing.
findings.independence: The Q2 Verizon 8-K reaffirming the range: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000732712/000073271226000040/a2026q2exhibit99.htm

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The negative lean agrees with the -24% 20-day run-up and the 52-week-low tape, so it is substantially priced; that is why p_up sits at 42 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 4/5 (financing is a question; covenant arithmetic is inference): the covenant finding was cut from -1.5 to -1.0. The answer to the question was covenant pressure with no corroborated ramp funding, so the sign stays negative.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): the Nokia IP/optical read-through was cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Rule 6 (inside the guide is a reported-quarter item): the guide-delivery track-record finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct kept at 15, slightly above the 13.75 median, and not shrunk. The Verizon guidance finding was left at -3.0.
